House rules

Edit only your own sections. To change someone else’s, tell them or open a pull request.
Write in your own words. The brief allows AI for proofreading only, not first drafts.
Model training lives in scripts (R/ or python/) that write to outputs/. The report only reads those files, so it renders in seconds. Commit the scripts too: that is what makes it reproducible.
Label figures and tables with your section key: eda, split, cnn, siam, tune, comp (e.g. fig-cnn-digit, tbl-siam-metrics). Cross-reference with @fig-cnn-digit and @sec-cnn.
Numbers in the text come from inline r code reading the output files, never typed by hand. They then stay correct when a model is re-run.
Guard every chunk that needs a file with #| eval: !expr ready("path").
Keep a note of your AI use per task as you go. It goes in the appendix table at the end.

7.3 Side by side






TipOwner: Maxine (Role A) · Task 6 · ≈ 400 words



Answer these:

With one script on the same test pairs, how do the PCA baseline, CNN and Siamese embeddings compare on AUC, equal error rate and nearest-centroid writer accuracy?
Which model suits which question (identify one of 20 known writers vs verify a pair), and what does each cost (e.g. retraining when a new writer is added)?
Do the digit rankings agree across the CNN, the Siamese network and the EDA?
How large is the session gap (same-session vs cross-session) for each model?
Critical caveats: simulated data, one test session, 20 writers.
